hot.title: Recursive Collective Intelligence: Emergence on an Equal-Budget Ladder in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
hot.summary: The authors test when multi-agent communication adds value beyond independent attempts at equal token cost. On HiddenBench, fact forwarding among four Qwen3.8-27B agents reaches 0.959 accuracy, 0.310 above compute-matched pass@n; the full-information agent scores 0.942. On held-out SplitBench tasks, recursive training improves the group’s margin from −0.253 at G0 to +0.159 at G2. These findings are limited to the tested settings.

hot.title: Verifiable On-Policy Distillation
hot.summary: The authors introduce Verifiable On-Policy Distillation (VOPD) for mathematical reasoning, using teacher–verifier agreement within groups of sampled responses to scale teacher guidance across next-token choices. VOPD compares teacher preferences with verified outcomes through a reference-model log-probability shift. In tests of two Qwen3 configurations and eight math benchmarks, it averages 66.38, above OPD and ExOPD, using the student’s top 16 tokens.

hot.title: OmniAct: One Policy, One Million Embodiments
hot.summary: OmniAct conditions a shared policy on each arm’s camera-relative joint geometry and predicts actions for its joints. In 2,000 simulated episodes with held-out embodiments and scenes, it achieves 63.0% success across six tasks at a 500-step cap, versus 57.9% for UMI all-views. Zero-shot, it succeeds in 13 of 20 OpenYAM setups, versus 7 for a baseline; evidence covers one arm and pick-and-place.

hot.title: Reinforcement Learning Can Be Recovered From Its Own Rollouts
hot.summary: The authors test whether supervised learning on archived reinforcement-learning responses can recover online reinforcement-learning progress. Chronological maximum-likelihood replay trains on saved correct and incorrect responses without reward labels. On Qwen3-1.7B-Base, it tracks MaxRL across four benchmarks, with mean absolute pass@k gaps of 0.2–1.1 percentage points. Results depend on setting: late batches nearly recover some endpoints, but not universally.

hot.title: Sample-Efficient In-Context Adaptation via Sleep
hot.summary: Sleep lets Transformer models refine their key-value cache at chunk boundaries, using recurrent passes over context already read. Rather than add depth to every generated token, the model updates its attention memory periodically, then resumes ordinary decoding. On held-out code, 1.2B-parameter models matched baseline loss with 2.10× fewer context tokens at N=2 and 2.39× at N=4; this measures prefix length, not speed.

hot.title: ThinkMorph-SSL: Scaling Interleaved Multimodal Reasoning with Pretext Tasks
hot.summary: ThinkMorph-SSL first trains multimodal models on image-derived restoration traces, then continues with task-specific demonstrations that use intermediate images to answer questions. This two-stage recipe improves average accuracy by 11.33 percentage points over BAGEL think-4k across 12 benchmarks, with gains on all 12. Nine benchmarks lie outside the instruction-tuning task families, but this does not establish that their image sources were unseen.

hot.title: EmbodiSafety: Benchmarking Risk Understanding and Response in Embodied AI
hot.summary: EmbodiSafety evaluates robot decisions in single-image Snapshot and ordered-frame Trajectory tasks across 1,632 decisions in 844 visual scenarios. It scores response mode, risk or uncertainty identification, and valid next action; Trajectory also tests recovery versus human escalation. Claude-Opus-5.5 leads reference models at 56.1% and 61.5% L3, measuring judged responses to generated scenes, not physical execution.

hot.title: Attention Latent Feedback
hot.summary: ALF (Attention Latent Feedback) lets each sublayer use the previous token’s outputs at its own and deeper layers, alongside a projected summary of the previous final state. Across three tested MoE sizes, it lowers held-out loss versus standard residual and final-state feedback. On MoE-4.0B, the four-domain average accuracy rises from 45.1% to 47.0% under teacher-forced scoring, not open-ended generation.

hot.title: An algebraic quantization of gravity from the null cone
hot.summary: Authors quantize gravity in a finite causal diamond by solving null-cone constraints and quantizing boundary data and a shear-sensitive clock. Shear delays reaching a fixed corner area, so a maximum clock reading selects a finite-dimensional sector. The trace yields the Bekenstein–Hawking area term and a one-loop logarithmic correction of 106/45 for a large Schwarzschild black hole at fixed mass, angular momenta summed.

hot.title: Monitoring the Paper Machine: AI Research in the Age of Acceleration
hot.summary: The authors build an observatory tracking AI research output and public traces from papers and repositories across 11 venues. It analyzes paper text, GitHub histories, and closed-model dependencies to assess how research is produced and whether evidence remains checkable. In 2025, 14.3% of papers at five venues depended on models announced for retirement; the measures do not show AI caused growth.

hot.title: Counterfactual Debugging the World Model Transfer Gap
hot.summary: The authors attribute real-world return gaps to consequential world-model transition errors. They replay trajectories with selected transitions replaced by world-model predictions, then use recursive, coarse-to-fine counterfactual Shapley attribution to focus computation on steps with non-negligible effects. In a planted MiniGrid test, the method recovered all causal steps through one million steps; this result depends on sparse causal errors and conditions.

hot.title: SpecEngineeringBench: Evaluating Coding Agents as Autonomous Specification Engineers
hot.summary: SpecEngineeringBench evaluates seven agent configurations on 100 instances from 78 open-source Python repositories. Agents use requirements and unmarked repositories to choose tests and investigation locations; tests are assessed on defective and repaired snapshots. They achieved 91.47% Head Pass Rate and 80.48% Change-focused Coverage, but 26.36% Fail-to-Pass Rate, showing these measures differ. Results describe this benchmark, not software verification generally.

hot.title: PyRUA-Dex: Learning Programmatic Policies for Dexterous Bimanual Manipulation with Coding Agents
hot.summary: PyRUA-Dex lets coding agents develop task-specific Python programs in simulation, then runs frozen programs without language-model calls at test time. Its refinement stage evaluates ordered task stages across randomized layouts and targets weak stages. On simulated Bench2Dex, it scores 72.9 versus 70.5 for ME-Dex 1.5, despite lower efficiency; results do not establish faster execution or broad hardware reliability.

hot.title: iWAM: Efficient Action Prediction from World Models without Explicit Future Prediction
hot.summary: iWAM helps robot policies use future-specific features without generating future video. During training, it links noise to a demonstrated future; at deployment, one video-model pass supplies features to the action policy. On unfamiliar DROID simulation tasks, its two-step MIP variant averages 91.7% success versus IDM’s 96.7%, while observation-only FastWAM averages 9.2%; this is not a general proof of robot performance.

hot.title: WebVibe: Multimodal Interactive Website Generation via Reverse Synthesis and Visual Self-Distillation
hot.summary: WebVibe and Interactive-SDPO train models for interactive multi-page website generation. WebVibe builds sites, verifies navigation and widget behavior in a browser, then derives training descriptions from passing sites. Interactive-SDPO adds replay traces and before-and-after screenshots to feedback-conditioned training. On Vision2Web L2, InteractiveCoder-9B reaches 55.15 FS versus 20.20 for its base; controlled ablations support the combined recipe, not either component alone.

hot.title: RoboUniverse-10K: Toward the Scaling Era of Agentic Robotics via Real-to-Sim Environments
hot.summary: RoboUniverse-10K turns real manipulation videos into simulated robot-training tasks by having coding agents build scenes, controllers, and verifiers, with an independent agent checking environments. Its 10,807 environments include 10,307 training tasks and 500 held-out tasks. GPT-6.2 Astra reaches 85.8% success on the held-out set, while simulated scenes remain simplified and tasks mostly short-horizon.

hot.title: DexWAC: A Unified World-Actor-Critic Model for Dexterous Robot Manipulation
hot.summary: DexWAC trains one system to propose robot actions, predict their endpoint effects, and estimate task progress. It jointly learns a shared context for an actor, world model, and temporal-difference critic. The world model predicts visual latents and proprioception at action-chunk endpoints. Across eight DexJoCo tasks, mean success is 65.50% before and 67.75% after PPO; physical-robot improvement remains untested.

hot.title: EgoUseBench: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agents under Evolving First-Person Contexts
hot.summary: EgoUseBench introduces a benchmark for testing whether agents can connect first-person observations and user requests to website actions. It compares six models across Computer-Use, Offline Ego Use, and Online Ego Use settings using tasks and final-state success. Mean success rates are 86.1%, 64.2%, and 63.4%, respectively; these results show a gap between tested settings, not that evolving context alone causes it.

hot.title: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer
hot.summary: U-MoLT improves validation quality and enables single-traversal decoding with shared Transformer layers. Mixture-of-Loops Attention reads sequence key–value memory and selected same-token layer memory; loop-KV feedback uses only earlier-token positions, allowing each new token to reuse cached prefix memory. After 400B tokens, its 3B MoE model improves mean 10-domain perplexity from 13.99 to 13.24. S-size latency is comparable to OLMo3 in one tested setup.

likes.title: Language Model Harnesses Can Be Compositional Generalizers
likes.summary: The paper trains a recursive language model harness to handle long tasks by keeping context outside the prompt, using code to inspect it, and delegating smaller queries to model calls. On eight held-out long-context benchmarks, RLM-27B averages 58.5 versus 46.1 for Qwen3.8-27B in the same harness; this is a benchmark-score gain, not a compute or time result.

likes.title: GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer
likes.summary: GLM-5.4 is Z.ai's first flagship model built on a Loop Transformer, which runs a weight-shared block of layers for multiple iterations to add reasoning depth without adding parameters. Rather than pre-training a looped model from scratch, Z.ai adapted the pre-trained GLM-5 base through continued training, looping 28 layers for two iterations at 750B scale. The post frames the model as the start of "Generalized Coding", where code generation extends to video, CAD, games, and 3D.

likes.title: A Claimed Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis
likes.summary: Levent Alpöge’s note describes a proposed route to the Riemann Hypothesis, using chained theta lifts to mimic multiplicity in Stepanov’s function-field method, which concerns a different setting. Alpöge reports Claude suggested a chain about √X long for a von Mangoldt sum of length X, and claims the approach extends to GRH; the note offers no readable proof or verification.

likes.title: Composable Soft-Prompt Distillation of RL Experts: Toward Continual Post-Training
likes.summary: CSPD turns reinforcement-learning specialists into independently trained soft prompts, keeping the pre-reinforcement-learning backbone frozen and concatenating selected prompts at inference. In a four-domain test with a Qwen3-4B student, the composed prompts raised the average score from 50.41 to 67.83, compared with 67.79 for MOPD. This result covers four tested domains, not broader scaling.

likes.title: Feedback Shortcut: Speculative Decoding for Latent Feedback Transformers
likes.summary: Feedback Shortcut enables speculative decoding for latent-feedback Transformers. It aligns multi-token prediction head states as feedback stand-ins, then recomputes pending positions during the next verification call. For a 780M model with three heads, one correction, and batch size 1, it reports 0.8287 BPB versus 0.8288 for exact decoding, and 2.75× throughput; this is single-GPU steady-state serving, not exact output equivalence.

likes.title: Language Model Harnesses can be Compositional Generalizers
likes.summary: The authors train an RLM harness using synthetic traces to improve transfer from shorter tasks to longer contexts. It keeps context outside the root prompt and uses programmatic calls to divide work among smaller inputs. In the same harness, fine-tuned Qwen3.8-27B reaches an eight-benchmark average of 58.5, versus 46.1 for the untrained model, with roughly half inference tokens; transfer is conditional.

likes.title: A CPU Inside an LLM: Zero-Gradient Compilation of Exact Circuits into Pretrained Weights
likes.summary: The authors graft a deterministic arithmetic circuit into pretrained model weights, enabling signed addition, subtraction, and multiplication without gradient updates, labeled examples, or runtime tool calls. Scale-robust circuit primitives and tokenizer-aligned emission let the language model resume after the answer. On Arith-1200, BF16 grafts reach 99.17% on Granite 4.2 3B and 100.00% on Qwen 3.5 4B, within the suite’s tested formats.

likes.title: Depth Pro 2: Sharp and Temporally Consistent Metric Monocular Depth
likes.summary: Depth Pro 2 estimates metric depth from images and video by processing frames jointly at native resolution with within-frame and cross-frame attention. In zero-shot comparisons, H+ ranks first for video metric-depth accuracy, boundary sharpness, and temporal consistency. On Sintel with predicted intrinsics, H+ reaches 41.4% δ1 versus 37.0% for UniDepthV2-L; rankings summarize separate measures, and results vary by model size.

likes.title: Mind2Act World: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Embodied Mind, Physical Action, and Mind-Action Composition in Robotic Manipulation
likes.summary: Mind2Act World tests whether robots use memory, execution, and feedback across related simulated tabletop tasks. It separates memory-focused Mind tasks, action-focused Act tasks, and workflows where outcomes guide later decisions. GPT-6 Astra succeeds on 52.7% of Mind episodes, 39.0% of Act episodes, and 12.0% of Mind2Act episodes. These task-set rates do not isolate composition as the cause, and physical-robot transfer remains unmeasured.

likes.title: Perplexity and Intelligence
likes.summary: Perplexity-based tracking measures language models’ pretraining progress through next-token prediction loss, and the post argues that it can provide a durable comparison metric as downstream benchmarks change. likes.title: Posterior Matching Distillation
likes.summary: Posterior Matching Distillation (PMD) trains a stochastic few-step image generator to preserve multiple plausible clean images for the same noisy input. It matches exponentially weighted student predictions to shifted-input targets from a frozen teacher under Gaussian corruption. On four-step FLUX.2 [klein] 4B, PMD reaches Vendi 3.3708 versus 2.4104 for SMD, with FID 24.12 versus 24.58 for the base model.

likes.title: Unlocking the Power of Loops in Pretrained LLMs with Loop Residuals
likes.summary: LoopRes lets pretrained language models reuse layers for additional computation by giving each reused layer access to recent intermediate results, with cues for their loop positions. On Qwen3-1.7B-Base, it scores 55.8 across seven math and code benchmarks at twice the compute per token of unlooped SFT, versus 43.2 for SFT; general-purpose performance remains untested.

likes.title: Pruning Autonomous Driving VLAs: What to Preserve for Reasoning and Action
likes.summary: MoOP compresses Alpamayo-1.5-10B by pruning a vision-language model (VLM) for both Chain-of-Causation explanations and trajectory generation. It ranks units using cross-entropy and flow-matching objectives, retaining VLM units important to either, and selects action-expert MLP channels across denoising steps. With VLM-only pruning at 24.0% total parameter reduction, it scores 68.8% on LingoQA versus 37.0% for FM-only; the dense model scores 73.2%, a difference from MoOP that is not statistically significant.

likes.title: Weight-Space Programming of JEPA World Models
likes.summary: The authors test whether an LLM can edit a world model from a description of changed physics, without new-system data or gradients. In two simulations, edits remap changed controls into controls the model understands, improving predictions and sometimes planning. On Push-T gain 20→60, error falls 90%, from 0.529 to 0.054; object-dynamics changes remain difficult, and prediction gains do not always improve planning.
